title: Spatial voice for very large virtual events
summary: Many people in one virtual space hear each other by where they stand: the shard forwards the nearest voices unchanged, mixes cell and sector beds once per frame (never per listener), and the device renders binaurally.

capacity.comment: Measured by `budget` (real libopus 0.3 / bundled C, release build) on a 4-core host, 5 % of listeners talking, 0.5 listeners/m2, 20 ms frames. Target: shard p99 < 20 ms and bed added latency (20 ms wait + p99) < 50 ms. A single shard of 50 000 listeners does NOT meet it on 4 cores (p99 96.6 ms, reports/budget-50000.json); the planner divides by the figures below. Update with every release.
capacity.load_bearing: Per-speaker decode (about 2 500 active at 50 000 listeners, ~21 ms p99 on 4 cores) and per-listener selection (~18-30 ms) are fixed by the crowd and scale with cores; the bed encode (cells) is the one knob: cell size 8 m -> 1 300 cells, 44 ms p99; 16 m -> 470 cells, 18 ms; 32 m -> 120 cells, 6 ms. Bed complexity 0 vs 3 saves ~8 ms at 16 m cells; bed bitrate 8 kbit/s saves bandwidth (167 vs 206 kbit/s per listener) but little CPU. So: shard by listeners per core (~2 500), widen cells to 16 m, do not try to fit 50 000 into one 4-core shard.
capacity.variance_note: p99 over 250 frames varies run to run on a shared host (e.g. 10 000 listeners / 16 m cells: 11.6-15.4 ms over 4 runs); 12 000 listeners reached 19.7 ms in one run, so 10 000 keeps the margin.

components.name: audio-shard
components.role: decodes active speakers, forwards near voices, mixes and encodes cell and sector beds; the `budget` binary is the acceptance harness, the serving binary is not part of this blueprint yet

components.name: client-core
components.role: render::Spatializer plus Opus decode: binaural rendering (ITD/ILD, distance, air absorption, reverb) on the device; 2.8 % of one host core for 12 streams (a phone core is slower, not measured)

edges.why: neighbouring shards exchange border beds; about 1.4 Mbit/s per link at 7 000 listeners per shard (scale::plan)

acceptance.name: budget
acceptance.note: real Opus, timed per frame; exit code 1 unless p99 < 20 ms and bed added latency < 50 ms

acceptance.name: small-scene
acceptance.note: tests/budget_small.rs: stream bound per listener, beds beyond the near field, finite times, codec state released after silence

portability.platform_apis: none: Opus is portable C compiled from source (cmake), everything else is Rust
portability.hardware: none: no GPU or special CPU feature; the shard scales with cores (rayon)
portability.formats: Opus packets over a datagram channel; a bed is an ordinary Opus stream; positions and levels travel beside the packet

migration.users: no user data is stored: shards keep only codec state, dropped after 2 s of silence
migration.providers: stateless shards behind any UDP/QUIC-capable host; moving is pointing clients at another address

limits: The media path needs datagrams (UDP/QUIC). The ct-agents channel forward is TCP and, according to ct-agent docs/channel.md, not released for production: it must not carry voice. A2A channels are suitable only for control and, at best, border-bed exchange between shards once a datagram channel exists.
One shard of 50 000 listeners does not reach p99 < 20 ms on this 4-core host (96.6 ms); the figure is cores-bound, so shard size above scales with cores.
The device cost was measured on the host CPU, not on a phone.
No serving binary: only the budget harness and the library exist.
threats: The shard decodes all active speakers, so it hears the audio: no end-to-end encryption on the bed path; forwarded near voices could be sealed end to end, beds cannot.
A client can claim a high voice level or a false position to be selected by many listeners; levels and positions are trusted from the device.
Positions of all speakers are visible to the shard.
